_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for Sai Life Sciences. Only material published on or before 30-Sep-2026; later items are in updates/later-facts.json.

global.src: AR FY26 MD&A (Fortune Business Insights; Grand View Research)

india.nearTermGrowth: CRDMO revenue growth forecast at 8-10% in FY2026-27 on lower biopharma funding

drivers: Innovators outsource more research and manufacturing; integrated CRO-CDMO partnerships gain relevance (Q4FY26 deck p.7).
Large pharma diversifies supply chains away from China ('geopolitical uncertainty and concerns around intellectual property', CEO, 7-Aug-2026).
Biotech funding recovering but skewed to mid-to-late stage assets; ~18 US biotech IPOs and several large acquisitions in 2026 (CEO).
Peptides beyond GLP-1 (three blockbuster peptide launches in 2026), ADCs/XDCs, oligonucleotides: new modalities need specialist capacity.

biosecure.status: Enacted on 18-Dec-2025 as Section 851 of the FY2026 NDAA. Unlike the 2024 bill it names no companies: 'biotechnology companies of concern' come from the Pentagon's 1260H list and a separate OMB process; OMB's first list is due within a year of enactment (by Dec-2026), followed by guidance and, for OMB-listed firms, a five-year wind-down of existing contracts. WuXi AppTec was added to the 1260H list in Jun-2026; a US court enjoined that designation on 7-Aug-2026.

industry.tariffs: Sai: 'no impact seen so far'; big pharma has taken its own steps to mitigate tariffs (Q4FY26 deck p.10). West Asia conflict raised input and logistics costs; Sai is seeking price revisions, 'though recoveries may not always be contemporaneous'.

street.note: Latest note found for each broker, standing on 30-Sep-2026. Three brokers disclose a method and all three use EV/EBITDA: HDFC Securities (29x Q3FY28E, primary PDF), JM Financial (32x Sep-27E EBITDA in its Nov-2025 note) and Jefferies (initiated on 27x FY27 pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA, Mar-2025; the multiples in its later notes were not in the sources we could read). moat.evidence: Discovery chemistry, biology, DMPK and toxicology in Hyderabad and Boston feed process R&D (Hyderabad, Manchester) and 700 KL of GMP manufacturing; ~65% of discovery customers buy more than one service; 17 launches supported in five years

19 of the top 25 pharma companies; >90% of revenue from returning customers; ~91% of CDMO revenue from large pharma (FY25, HSIE); five of six recent late-phase additions came through dedicated-team (FTE) contracts
USFDA and PMDA inspections cleared at all R&D and manufacturing sites; PSCI audits; EcoVadis Platinum (2026)
700 KL, rising to ~1,150 KL in FY27 and a ~1,400 KL greenfield later: still a fraction of Divi's or Laurus; capacity has been a constraint (discovery facility sold out on opening)
Top customer 12.2% of FY26 revenue (two customers 21.5% in FY25); 33-34 commercial molecules; but quarterly CDMO revenue swings with a few campaigns (Q1FY27 +6%)
~4% of revenue; commercial peptide plant only in 2028; no biologics or mAb capability ('we will discuss this strategy at a later point')

critiques: The street's EPS looks too high: the FY27 capex guide (Rs1,100-1,300 cr) is roughly double FY26 and more than operating cash flow, so Sai moves from ~zero net debt to several hundred crore of borrowing; HDFC Securities' Jan-2026 model assumed ~Rs530 cr of capex and flat interest of ~Rs40 cr a year.

Valuation is stretched on any trailing basis: ~88x trailing P/E and ~46x trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close (Screener); the stock nearly doubled in eight months (Rs795 on 23-Jan-2026 to Rs1,524.5) while most targets lagged the price.
CDMO growth slowed to 6% in Q1FY27 after +33% in FY26; management asks investors to judge it over three to five years and guides only 15-20% a year.
FY26 margin had help: a Rs34 cr provision reversal and Rs30 cr of forex gains (in company EBITDA); underlying company margin was ~27.5%, below the 28-30% guide.
Returns are ordinary for the multiple: ROE 14% and ROCE 18% in FY26 (MD&A), and capital intensity is rising again; heavy capex ahead of demand risks under-utilisation (65% in Q1FY27).
Governance: the MD & CEO's pay rose 124% to Rs13.1 cr (231x the median employee) in the first full listed year.
BIOSECURE helps the narrative more than the numbers so far: the enacted law names no Chinese CDMO, WuXi's 1260H listing was enjoined in Aug-2026, and OMB's list is due only in Dec-2026.
Pipeline disclosure is thin: no customer or molecule names, no revenue per molecule; 'over 90% visibility' on FY27 is not a number investors can test.
gaps: Q4FY26, Q3FY26, Q2FY26 and Q1FY26 call transcripts not read (the company-hosted Q4FY26 link returned 'page not found'); Q4FY26 commentary taken from the deck.

Broker notes: only HDFC Securities' note read in full; Jefferies, JM Financial, Kotak and Morgan Stanley from secondary reports and trackers; the multiples behind Jefferies' Rs1,610 and JM's Rs1,318, and Kotak's and Morgan Stanley's methods, are not known.
No FY22-FY23 CDMO/CRO split (prospectus not read); quarterly split disclosed only for Q1FY27.
The Sep-2025 half-year balance sheet was not read: the EV/EBITDA history uses the Mar-2025 and Mar-2026 net cash (a gap of ~Rs170 cr, under 1% of EV).
No customer or molecule names, no revenue per molecule, utilisation only for Q1FY27 (65%).
Exact FY28 capex not guided (we assume Rs900 cr); Choutuppal project cost not disclosed.
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA (Jefferies' basis) not computed; we use reported (post-Ind AS) EBITDA with lease liabilities in net debt.
Promoter-group holdings beyond the eight named promoters (Screener 34.5% vs ~29.2% named) not itemised.
conflicts: Q1FY27 CRO growth: 24% (deck, press release) vs 26% (CEO/CFO on the call); revenue Rs553 cr (call) vs Rs554 cr (deck). We use the deck.
FY26 CDMO revenue: Rs1,417 cr in the deck (includes other operating income) vs Rs1,361.5 cr in the audited note; CRO Rs775 cr in both.
Tracker pages attribute the Rs1,450 (10-Aug-2026) and Rs1,160 (8-Apr-2026) targets to Kotak and Morgan Stanley inconsistently.
A Mar-2026 article cites '47x FY27' next to Jefferies' Rs1,300 target; Jefferies' initiation valued Sai on EV/EBITDA, and we read 47x as the stock's own multiple, not the target basis.
Company EBITDA FY26 Rs661 cr (incl. Rs30 cr forex) vs Screener Rs634 cr (forex in other income).
